column2: Docs current and consistent with the code [SO2]
column6: The five documents this criterion covers (docs/requirements.md, docs/design.md, README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, and the AI context file, such as AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md) exist, are in the PDF matching the named commit, and pass the spot-check: docs/design.md describes the system that exists, and docs/requirements.md carries acceptance criteria for current priorities and lists under Constraints the limits the team did not choose. Whether the README.md quickstart runs is scored under Build health.
column9: One of the five is missing or has drifted from the code, or they are missing sections, missing from the PDF (unless an NDA walkthrough stands in), or not rendered.
column12: Two or more of the five are missing or have drifted from the code, the PDF carries none of them without an NDA walkthrough standing in, or the documents in the PDF do not match the named commit (a sanitized PDF differs only in what was redacted).

column6: docs/rfcs/ or docs/adr/ records each decision with its outcome and the options rejected, and docs/risks.md is the single risk register, changed since the last checkpoint, ranked, and with owners; both are in the PDF matching the named commit, and no duplicate register exists elsewhere.
column9: Decisions and risks are tracked but incompletely: some decisions unrecorded, ranking or owners missing on some entries, the register has not changed since the last checkpoint, a second register exists, or one of the two is missing from the PDF or does not match the named commit (unless an NDA walkthrough stands in).
column12: No recorded decisions, no docs/risks.md or an empty one, or a register with neither ranking nor owners, or both are missing from the PDF or do not match the named commit (unless an NDA walkthrough stands in).

column6: CI passed on the named commit and runs the tests on every pull request (for a FOSS project, upstream's CI on your pull requests, or the build-and-test command your fork documents until your first one); at least one test would fail if the feature it covers broke; a grader can follow the quickstart cold. The checks match how much the team delegates: review gates on the changes that are expensive to undo (schema, authentication, deployment, migrations), changes exercised somewhere other than production before they reach users (a staging or preview environment, a store beta track, a dedicated test device, a run on sample data), and a documented rollback path.
column9: CI and tests exist, but the quickstart runs only with a step README.md does not give, or the checks have visible gaps relative to how the team works: no gate on a hard-to-undo path, nowhere to exercise changes before they reach users, or no documented rollback path.
column12: CI is absent or red, no test would fail if the feature it covers broke, the quickstart does not work, or changes reach production with no gate and no rollback path.

column2: Contribution traceability and version control hygiene [SO5]
column6: Each student's work is attributable over the period: code through reviewed PRs under real accounts, other work where CONTRIBUTING.md says it lives, and the Contribution lines in the sprint notes match that record. The history is one a maintainer could inherit: nothing lands on the default branch outside a pull request; no live secrets, build artifacts, or dependency directories are in the history (if a secret leaked, it was revoked or rotated, and the commit that removed it says so); commit messages say what changed and why, with noisy branches squashed on merge; nobody force-pushes the default branch; and large binaries are out of Git or in Git LFS.
column9: Most students' work is traceable, but some of it cannot be attributed, or the history misses one of those items (direct commits to the default branch, committed build artifacts or dependency directories, commit messages that do not say what changed and why, noisy branches merged unsquashed, a force-push to the default branch, large binaries outside Git LFS).
column12: Contribution cannot be traced to individuals over the period, or a secret was committed and never rotated.

column6: Every milestone item for this checkpoint is met: the stories docs/requirements.md marks for this term run end to end at the named commit against real components rather than stubs, the CI run linked on the cover ran the tests on the named commit including a test for at least one of those stories, docs/risks.md gives a real-user session's week, the participant's role, and who confirmed it, and the Definition of Done and the pull request and review rules in CONTRIBUTING.md changed since Repo Checkpoint 2 or say the refresh kept them.
column9: One milestone item is unmet or only demonstrable with help, and docs/risks.md gives an owner and a week to close it (e.g., one marked story still runs against a stub, no test covers a marked story, the real-user session is planned but has no week or participant yet, or CONTRIBUTING.md neither changed since Repo Checkpoint 2 nor says the refresh kept it).
column12: Two or more milestone items are unmet, or one is unmet with no docs/risks.md entry giving an owner and a week to close it.
